title: Setting Up Office Hours That Actually Get Used
summary: Set up IB office hours students will use from September to November, with practical scheduling, triage, boundaries, and follow-up systems for teachers.
body_markdown:
September-November is often the most congested part of the **IB teacher fall term** . Coursework checkpoints, Extended Essay meetings, TOK work, assessments, references, and ordinary teaching compete for limited time. Setting up office hours that get used therefore requires more than publishing an open-door slot.


The most effective model is a **structured support clinic** . Give each session a named focus, combine brief appointments with drop-ins, ask students to bring evidence of an attempt, and finish with one recorded next step.


### Why traditional office hours remain empty


Students may not understand what office hours are for. Some assume they should attend only when failing, while others think they need a sophisticated question before entering. An empty room does not necessarily indicate that nobody needs help.


Research from higher education cannot be transferred automatically to secondary IB settings, but it identifies useful barriers. In one[study of student motivations and barriers](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9727601/) , **40.9%** of respondents reported a direct timetable conflict, while others described intimidation or uncertainty. The[University of Wisconsin-Madison's inclusive office-hours guidance](https://idc.ls.wisc.edu/effective-inclusive-office-hours/) also recommends explaining the purpose, varying access, and structuring sessions.


Common barriers include:


- **Timing:** The slot conflicts with transport, CAS, activities, or another teacher.
- **Ambiguity:** “Come if you need help” does not explain what support is available.
- **Social risk:** Attending may feel like admitting failure.
- **Poor expected value:** General advice may not justify sacrificing scarce time.


### Start with the school assessment calendar


Obtain the shared DP calendar before selecting times. Mark IA checkpoints, EE meetings, TOK deadlines, reporting periods, mock examinations, and weeks when several subjects demand substantial work.


Do not treat an online date as a universal student deadline. The IB communicates submission dates to schools, while schools establish earlier internal schedules for supervision and administration. Official pages recommend staged internal deadlines for the[Extended Essay](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/extended-essay/submission-deadline/) and[TOK assessment components](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/theory-of-knowledge/upload-deadline/) .


Period Likely student need Useful office-hours focus


Early September Re-establish routines and identify gaps Diagnostic questions and research-question checks


Late September-October Manage overlapping drafts and tests IA methods, analysis, and targeted reteaching


Late October Respond appropriately to feedback Criterion interpretation and revision planning


November Prepare for school assessments Timed practice, error analysis, and permitted coursework questions


Adapt this pattern to the school calendar, current subject guide, and examination session. November-session candidates require a different plan from students earlier in the May-session cycle.


### Build a two-lane office-hours system


Use two access routes instead of one long open session.


### Lane 1: Short appointments


Offer **8-12 minute appointments** for private or student-specific issues. Suitable topics include an individual IA decision, a misconception revealed by assessment, a missed checkpoint, or a wellbeing concern.


Require students to select a category when booking, such as concept clarification, coursework planning, feedback interpretation, assessment review, or workload planning. This helps the teacher prepare and discourages vague requests.


### Lane 2: Open group clinics


Use the remaining time for a named clinic, such as “Economics evaluation clinic” or “Biology data-processing questions.” Students learn from shared questions, while the teacher avoids repeating the same explanation.


Keep individual marks and sensitive feedback private. Group clinics should address transferable skills, general requirements, or anonymized examples rather than publicly evaluating one student's work.


### Give every session a concrete promise


“Office hours, Tuesday lunchtime” communicates logistics but not value. State what students should bring and what they can expect to leave with:


> Tuesday IA clinic: bring one graph and the paragraph interpreting it. You will leave with one criterion-linked revision priority. Drop in from 12:35-12:55 or reserve a 10-minute slot.


Publish the focus in the same place each week, ideally the learning platform students already use. Mention it in class 24-48 hours beforehand and privately invite students whose recent work shows a relevant need.


### Require a small entry task


Preparation should be brief but visible. Ask students to bring:


1. The exact question, paragraph, calculation, or criterion causing difficulty.
2. Evidence of one genuine attempt.
3. A sentence beginning, “I think the problem is...”
4. The next deadline connected to the issue.


For exam support, the attempt might be one completed practice question. RevisionDojo's[teacher and department resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-for-ib-teachers-departments) and[school platform](https://www.revisiondojo.com/schools) can support targeted Questionbank assignments and Study Notes. Teacher time can then focus on why marks were lost rather than repeating content the student has not attempted.


### Protect feedback and academic-integrity boundaries


Office hours must not become unlimited editing. The IB's[academic integrity policy](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/shared-resources/pdfs/academic-integrity-policy-en.pdf) requires teachers to provide appropriate feedback without completing or excessively editing student work. Exact permissions depend on the component, current subject guide, and school policy.


During coursework conferences, teachers can protect student ownership by:


- Asking the student to explain their decision
- Referring to the relevant criterion or requirement
- Identifying a problem without supplying replacement prose
- Asking what evidence would demonstrate improvement
- Recording the meeting and agreed action


Avoid rewriting sentences, choosing conclusions, or repeatedly correcting a nearly final submission. RevisionDojo's guide to[delivering focused IA feedback](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-ib-teachers-can-deliver-better-ia-feedback-in-less-time) offers a priority model, but official guidance remains controlling. Suggestions from the[IB Coursework Grader](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grader) are diagnostic, not official marks or permission to exceed feedback limits.


### Use triage when demand spikes


When many students arrive before one deadline, begin with a two-minute triage:


- **Red:** A fundamental misconception, access issue, or safeguarding concern.
- **Amber:** A genuine attempt requiring one decision to be clarified.
- **Green:** A question suited to a shared example, resource, or peer discussion.


Handle red cases privately, group amber questions by theme, and direct green cases to the appropriate resource before checking understanding. Jojo AI or Study Notes can support routine concept clarification, preserving teacher time for decisions requiring knowledge of the student or school context.


### Measure use, not just attendance


For four weeks, record the date, focus, attendance, recurring misconception, and next action. Attendance alone can mislead because three prepared students may make more progress than a crowded but passive group.


Track whether students arrive with attempts, complete agreed actions, and repeat the same misunderstandings. If attendance is low, change one variable, such as timing, session title, length, or booking method. If attendance is high but progress remains weak, narrow the focus and strengthen the entry task.


### Conclusion


Effective September-November office hours are predictable, specific, and bounded. Plan around the school calendar, combine appointments with group clinics, require a modest attempt, and finish with one student-owned action.


RevisionDojo can support pre-clinic Questionbank practice, Study Notes, Jojo AI, and coursework diagnostics. Teachers should retain responsibility for official guidance, feedback limits, and professional judgment.
